methods: Checked each entry’s source-linked excerpt, place, coordinates, query and precision against its stated geographic scope.
Used public NYC DCP LION street endpoints and shared node topology in EPSG:4326 for current intersections; used centerlines for representative avenues.
Used NYC Parks polygons exposed by NYC DCP for park membership; used DCP GeoSearch PAD address matches for named institutions and 2020 NTA polygons for broad neighborhoods.
Small offsets consistent with stated representative scope were retained instead of changing every point.
Historical coastline, railway alignment, fictional addresses and vanished structures were not inferred from present-day GIS.
limitations: This is a 43-entry editorial geography audit, not 43 survey-precise or historically reconstructed scene locations.
Fulton Ferry operator reference returned HTTP 403 on re-fetch; its broad existing historical waterfront association was retained, not independently resurveyed.
The Battery park ownership polygon and Spuyten Duyvil land-only NTA query do not independently establish an exact point; both remain approximate waterfront/approach references.
Warren/Hudson is preserved as the novel’s wording, with nearby current Warren/West Broadway explicitly labeled an orientation point. No historical intersection or property transaction is certified.
No Google Cloud billing or API restrictions were inspected or changed. The website continues to use only the no-charge Embed endpoint and keyless Maps URLs.
